notes:
Shared contract for card messages (RFC 082), the v2.0 parts: the card `header` and the `Markdown`, `Fields` and `Divider` elements (RFC 082 §4.8). botiverse/slock packages/shared/src/messageCard.ts and messageCardMarkdown.ts; this file is pinned by messageCard.v1.vector.sha256. Compare as JSON values: key order is irrelevant, an absent key differs from a null one.
schemaVersion 1 (2026-11-05): Markdown links take a message's schemes, http:, https: and mailto: (Tenny, #13224): bare and angle email autolinks and [x](mailto:…) are allowed; tel: and sms: are refused.
display (markdown[], schemaVersion 1, 2026-11-05; Tenny, #proj-apps:#49 0994342b): a case with "display": "may_differ" holds one of the three constructs RFC 082 §4.8 lets clients display differently: 4-space indentation, an undefined reference ([ref], [text][ref], [^ref] with no definition), character entities (&, <, ©, B, ...). The Server's verdict and agentText stay exact. A client checks such a case against the rule, not against `nodes` and `text`: it shows all of the content (every run of letters and digits in `text` appears in what it shows, in order; the construct's own characters, such as an entity as written or the brackets, may be shown too), it shows no link, no button and no mention chip, and nothing it shows is outside the allowlist (an indented code block drawn as a code block is a code block, which is in it). Every case without `display` is compared exactly. No other client difference is allowed.
cards[]: `card` is what a sender sends. `verdict` is the Server's: accept or refuse (400 card_invalid with `problem.path` and `problem.limit`; `problem.node` with limit markdown). On accept: `parsed` is the stored card (defaults filled in: Fields mono false, and the v1 defaults); `agentText` is renderMessageCardMarkdown (what agents read under `card:`, at most 4000 code points); `fallback` is the content Raft stores when the sender wrote none (the same rendering, at most 500 code points, cut with …), or null with `fallbackProblem` when the card has nothing to derive it from (then the sender must write content). A client reads a stored card with the strict schema: every accepted card here is one a client must draw in full (the header, Markdown, Fields, Divider), and one it does not know must make it show the whole fallback, never part of the card.
markdown[]: `content` is one Markdown element's content in { version: 1, root: "m", elements: { m: { type: "Markdown", props: { content } } } }. The parser is CommonMark + GFM (micromark / mdast-util-from-markdown with GFM, as remark-parse + remark-gfm), with Raft math ($…$ and $$…$$, not money), CJK-friendly emphasis, and indented code off. The allowlist (node types): paragraph, text, break, strong, emphasis, delete, inlineCode, code (fenced), list, listItem (not a task list item), blockquote, link (http:, https: or mailto:, case-insensitive, the schemes a message's links take, so GFM's email autolinks are links; a link must parse as a URL). Lists and quotes together nest at most 3 levels. On refuse: `found` lists every node outside it, outermost first, in document order (nothing inside one is looked at): `node` (the mdast type; taskListItem for a GFM task list item; link for a link to another scheme, such as tel: or sms:; list or blockquote nested too deep), its `source` slice, `line` and `column` (1-based); the Server refuses with the first. A client draws each `found` node as its `source` text (never rendered) and the rest as Markdown; its own parser must find the same nodes. On accept: `nodes` are the node types in the tree (root aside, sorted), `text` the values of its text, inlineCode and code nodes in order with a line break for each break node (what a reader sees, entities decoded), and `agentText` the agent text. No @name or #channel in Markdown is a mention or a channel link: clients draw no chips in it.

markdown.name: line_breaks

markdown.name: fenced_math_is_code
markdown.note: A ```math fence is a code block: clients draw it as code, never as a formula.

markdown.name: indented_is_text
markdown.note: Indented code is off, as in chat: four spaces of indentation are a paragraph (plain CommonMark would make a code block). Allowed difference 1 (RFC 082 §4.8): a client may draw a code block.

markdown.name: cjk_emphasis
markdown.note: CJK-friendly emphasis: `**中文**的` is bold before a CJK character (plain CommonMark leaves the stars as text).

markdown.name: intraword_underscore

markdown.name: lists

markdown.name: nesting_3_mixed

markdown.name: nesting_4_mixed

markdown.name: autolink_angle_https
markdown.note: A CommonMark autolink to https: is a link.

markdown.name: autolink_literal_https
markdown.note: A bare https URL is a link (GFM); the sentence's full stop is not part of it.

markdown.name: autolink_literal_www
markdown.note: A bare www. address is an http: link (GFM).

markdown.name: autolink_literal_trailing_paren
markdown.note: A bare URL in parentheses ends before the closing parenthesis (GFM).

markdown.name: autolink_angle_with_at
markdown.note: An @ inside an angle autolink is part of the link.

markdown.name: autolink_literal_url_with_at
markdown.note: An @ inside a URL is part of the link, not a mention.

markdown.name: autolink_angle_mailto
markdown.note: <mailto:…> is a mailto: link, a scheme a message's links take: allowed.

markdown.name: autolink_angle_email
markdown.note: <a@b.c> is an email autolink, a mailto: link: allowed, as in a message.

markdown.name: autolink_literal_email
markdown.note: A bare email address is a mailto: link (GFM): allowed, as in a message.

markdown.name: autolink_angle_tel
markdown.note: <tel:…> is a link to tel:: refused (links are http:, https: or mailto:).

markdown.name: autolink_angle_other_scheme
markdown.note: <custom:x> is a link to custom:: refused.

markdown.name: link_mailto
markdown.note: A mailto: link is allowed, as in a message.

markdown.name: link_tel
markdown.note: A tel: link is refused: links are http:, https: or mailto:.

markdown.name: link_sms
markdown.note: An sms: link is refused: links are http:, https: or mailto:.

markdown.name: link_javascript
markdown.note: Links are http:, https: and mailto: only.

markdown.name: link_relative
markdown.note: A relative link has no scheme: refused.

markdown.name: link_fragment
markdown.note: A fragment-only link has no scheme: refused.

markdown.name: link_scheme_case
markdown.note: Schemes are case-insensitive.

markdown.name: link_title
markdown.note: A link with a title is a link.

markdown.name: entities_text
markdown.note: Character references are text: `<div>` shows `<div>`, never an element; `&` shows `&`. Allowed difference 3 (RFC 082 §4.8): a client may show an entity as written.

markdown.name: entities_numeric
markdown.note: Numeric character references, decimal and hex, and a named one in a word: text. Allowed difference 3 (RFC 082 §4.8): a client may show an entity as written.

markdown.name: bare_lt_amp
markdown.note: A `<` or `&` that starts no tag or reference is text.

markdown.name: almost_html_lt3
markdown.note: Lines that are almost HTML stay text: `<3`, `a<b`, `< b>`, `<1st>`.

markdown.name: almost_html_unclosed
markdown.note: An unclosed `<tag` is text.

markdown.name: html_generic_type
markdown.note: `<String>` is an HTML tag to CommonMark: refused; write it as inline code.

markdown.name: html_inline
markdown.note: Inline HTML: refused (each tag found).

markdown.name: html_block
markdown.note: Block HTML: refused.

markdown.name: html_comment
markdown.note: An HTML comment: refused.

markdown.name: html_escaped
markdown.note: An escaped `<` is text.

markdown.name: heading_atx
markdown.note: A heading: refused.

markdown.name: heading_setext
markdown.note: A setext heading: refused.

markdown.name: thematic_break
markdown.note: A horizontal rule: refused (a Divider element draws one).

markdown.name: dash_rule_after_paragraph
markdown.note: `---` under a line makes it a heading: refused.

markdown.name: image
markdown.note: An image: refused.

markdown.name: table
markdown.note: A table: refused.

markdown.name: footnote
markdown.note: A footnote: refused (the reference is found first).

markdown.name: reference_link
markdown.note: A reference-style link: refused (the reference is found first).

markdown.name: definition_alone
markdown.note: A link reference definition: refused.

markdown.name: brackets_without_definition
markdown.note: `[x]` with no definition is text, as are `[x][y]` and `[^1]` with none. Allowed difference 2 (RFC 082 §4.8): a client may draw an undefined reference differently, never as a link.

markdown.name: math_inline
markdown.note: Inline math: refused.

markdown.name: math_block
markdown.note: Display math: refused.

markdown.name: dollars_money
markdown.note: Money is not math: `$5 to $10` stays text.

markdown.name: task_list
markdown.note: A task list item (GFM): refused.

markdown.name: mentions_in_text
markdown.note: `@name`, an escaped `\@name` and `@name` are text; the agent text sets each as inline code (an `@` the Server's parser reads, as in `a\@b`, or the web's chips read, as in `@name` and `_@name_`), so no reader takes it for a mention. It holds a character entity (`@`): allowed difference 3 (RFC 082 §4.8).

markdown.name: mentions_next_to_code
markdown.note: An @name next to a backtick stays apart from it in the agent text; an unpaired backtick pairs with nothing.

markdown.name: channel_refs_text
markdown.note: `#channel` is text: no channel link.
